FAA Approves Trump Arch Near D.C. Airport After Flight Path Review

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has approved the construction of a planned arch near Reagan National Airport in Washington D.C. The arch is intended to be a triumphal monument. Initial concerns were raised about the structure's proximity to the airport's primary approach and departure corridor, situated 3,000 feet from the airfield. However, the FAA has stated that the arch will not interfere with flight paths after making one adjustment. The approval came after a review process addressing potential risks to commercial flights.
